entrada.texto: Verifiable Credentials: Transforming Digital Identity in the Real World | IJSRCSEIT Skip to main content Skip to main navigation menu Skip to site footer Open Menu Home Current Archives Archives Conferences Editorial Board Editorial Team Reviewers Board Reviewers Responsibilities Editors Responsibilities Editorial Board Member Selection Process For Author Peer Review Policy Manuscript Types Abstracting and Indexing Research and Publication Ethics CrossMark Policy Guidelines for Authors Author's Responsibilities Copyright and licensing Digital archiving Awards Awards & Recognitions Upcoming Award Event Past Award events About Open Access Policy About the Journal Contact Aims & Scope Publisher business practices Search Register Login Home / Archives / Vol. 11 No. 2 (2025): March-April / Research Articles Verifiable Credentials: Transforming Digital Identity in the Real World Authors Ravikanth Reddy Gudipati University at Buffalo, USA DOI: https://doi.org/10.32628/CSEIT25112382 Abstract This comprehensive article explores the transformative impact of Verifiable Credentials (VCs) in revolutionizing digital identity management across various sectors. The article examines the core components, technical architecture, and real-world implementations of VC systems, highlighting their role in enhancing security, privacy, and operational efficiency. The article investigates adoption challenges and solutions, focusing on enterprise integration and regulatory compliance. Additionally, it explores emerging technologies, including AI integration and post-quantum security, along with government initiatives shaping the future of digital identity. The article demonstrates that VCs offer a paradigm shift in how organizations approach identity verification, enabling secure, privacy-preserving, and decentralized credential management while significantly reducing administrative overhead and fraud risks. resposta.resumo: O artigo apresenta as Verifiable Credentials (VCs) como tecnologia que transforma a gestão de identidade digital, proporcionando segurança, privacidade e descentralização. Descreve a arquitetura técnica, casos de uso reais e destaca a redução de custos administrativos e fraudes. Também discute desafios de adoção, integração empresarial e conformidade regulatória, além de apontar tendências como IA, segurança pós‑quântica e iniciativas governamentais.

perfil.solucao: Verifiable Credentials (VCs) enable secure, privacy‑preserving, and decentralized credential management
perfil.avaliacao: significantly reducing administrative overhead and fraud risks
perfil.possibilidades: Explorar a aplicação de VCs para controle de acesso em IoT de cidades inteligentes; combinar VCs com criptografia baseada em atributos (ABE) para compartilhamento de dados sensíveis; avaliar desempenho e escalabilidade em ambientes de edge computing; analisar requisitos regulatórios para identidade digital no setor público; investigar a integração de segurança pós‑quântica em VCs para IIoT.
